title: 2027 Grammy nominations release today. Here's what you need to know
summary: Nominations for the 69th Grammy Awards are scheduled to be announced today, broadcast live from New York's Time Square on Grammy.com and the Grammys' YouTube channel.

image.caption: Nominations for the 69th Grammy Awards are scheduled to be announced today, broadcasting live from New York's Time Square on Grammy.com and the Grammys YouTube channel. (Robyn Beck/AFP/Getty Images)

blocks.text: Nominations for the 69th Grammy Awards are scheduled to be announced today, broadcast live from New York's Time Square on Grammy.com and the Grammys' YouTube channel.
Nominations for 69th annual Grammy Awards to broadcast live at 7:45 a.m. ET
Nominations for the 69th Grammy Awards are scheduled to be announced today, broadcasting live from New York's Time Square on Grammy.com and the Grammys YouTube channel.

The annual honours will start at 7:45 a.m. ET before a wrap-up show at 9 a.m. ET, the latter of which will highlight select nominees. Scheduled presenters for the main show include Alan Menken, David Guetta, Linda Perry, Herbie Hancock, Olivia Dean, Pharrell Williams, Yungblud and Renée Fleming.
This year, the awards boast five new categories and brand new eligibility rules. Those changes will partially shape the slate of performers announced today, particularly in the new artist category.

There, artists are now allowed to submit for that category four times throughout their career instead of three; according to Billboard, that opens up the opportunity for potential front-runners Ella Langley and Megan Moroney, who otherwise would be ineligible this year.

Meanwhile, there are five entirely new categories this year: best Latin song, best traditional folk album, best traditional pop vocal performance, best R&B collaboration or duo/group performance and best Asian pop music performance. The last addition struck a sour note with some music fans and creators — particularly in the K-pop space.
BTS won’t enter the 2027 Grammy Awards
A month after the Recording Academy, which organizes the Grammys, announced the new awards space, powerhouse group BTS shared a joint statement saying they would not submit their music.

“We hope our music can be heard and loved for what it is, rather than being divided by region or language,” the co-ordinated message read. “We thank [fanbase] Army and everyone who has always stood by us.”

Some fans viewed the new category as a racialized barrier for Asian performers — especially so soon after Golden from the film Kpop Demon Hunters became the first K-pop song to win a Grammy earlier this year. The Grammys caused similar controversy when they split up the country album category into "traditional" and "contemporary" after Beyoncé became the first Black artist to win best country album in 2025.

The new Latin song category also reflects the growing popularity of that genre. At the 68th Grammy Awards, Bad Bunny's DeBÍ TiRAR MáS FOToS became the first all-Spanish release to win album of the year, the night's highest honour.

Today's nominations come shortly after the 27th annual Latin Grammy Awards, which saw Spanish singer Rosalía win album of the year on Thursday. The 69th Grammy Awards themselves will take place Feb. 7, 2027, on ABC and stream on Disney+ and Hulu, live from Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles.
Jackson Weaver is a reporter and film critic for CBC's entertainment news team in Toronto. You can reach him at jackson.weaver@cbc.ca.
